liner.body_md:
## What listeners single out

- **Friend of the Devil** (1 review): Phil's bass seems missing elsewhere on the soundboard, but the reviewer hears him in this song [9]
- **Saint Of Circumstance** (1 review): The band adds a small jam twist at the end of the song [14]
- **U. S. Blues** (1 other source): Notes list U.S. Blues as the encore, after Good Lovin' [1]
- **Scarlet Begonias** (1 review): Jerry hits the effects pedal right after the last line, earlier than usual going into Fire [12]
- **Fire On The Mountain** (1 review): Scarlet>Fire is tight and well recorded, with no jam out of Fire, going straight into drums [14]
- **The Wheel** (1 review): Reviewer says it was the first Wheel in some time, and the first with Brent [12]

## The recordings

- **gd80-08-17.aud.munder.12107.sbeok.shnf** (recommended): audience recording; 21 songs; 148 min; rated 4/5 by 2 [1]. Said about its sound: Reviewer hears stage technical difficulties and finds the audience source only middling [3]
- **gd1980-08-17.sbd.miller.93037.sbeok.flac16**: soundboard; 21 songs; 140 min; rated 3.5/5 by 10 [2]. Said about its sound: Jerry's guitar sits very low in the mix for most of the first set; Soundboard has plenty of sound, better than the average soundboard from any era; Sound has problems early in the second set, then improves in the middle of Samson And Delilah [2][6][14]

## Around the show

- Reviewer drove 200 miles to attend the show [4]
- Reviewer calls this summer tour among the most undercirculated, with many shows surfacing late in the digital era [6]
- Show flies under the radar because the late-summer 1980 tour had many other standout shows [12]

## Tapers and lineage

- **gd80-08-17.aud.munder.12107.sbeok.shnf**: source: Audience Recording [1]. Also: Audience recording, passed through an unknown generation to CD, supplied via Paul B and seeded to etree by Willy; Reviewer taped the show from the 17th row with a small 'toy' recorder [1][4]
- **gd1980-08-17.sbd.miller.93037.sbeok.flac16**: transferred by Charlie Miller; source: SBD -> Cassette Master -> Reel -> Dat (48k) [2]. Also: Soundboard transfer from Rob Eaton's lent DATs, with pitch correction; original mics unknown, cassette master; A cassette fills gaps: all of Don't Ease Me In and the first couple of minutes of Samson And Delilah [2]
